title: Computational Astrophysics: Polytropes & Interactive HR Diagram
Computational Astrophysics: Polytropes & Interactive HR Diagram
Computational Astrophysics: Polytropes & Interactive HR Diagram
text:
2. Fortran 90: High-Performance Lane-Emden Equation Solver
The Lane-Emden equation governs the dimensionless density profile \(\theta(\xi)\) of self-gravitating polytropic fluid spheres (\(P = K \rho^{1 + 1/n}\)): \[\frac{1}{\xi^2} \frac{d}{d\xi}\left( \xi^2 \frac{d\theta}{d\xi} \right) + \theta^n = 0\]
Boundary conditions at the stellar center (\(\xi = 0\)) are \(\theta(0) = 1\) and \(\theta'(0) = 0\).
! lane_emden.f90
! Compile: gfortran -O3 -std=f2018 lane_emden.f90 -o lane_emden
program solve_lane_emden
    implicit none
    integer, parameter :: dp = kind(1.0d0)
    real(dp) :: xi, theta, phi, dxi, xi_max, n_poly
    real(dp) :: k1_th, k1_ph, k2_th, k2_ph, k3_th, k3_ph, k4_th, k4_ph
    integer :: step, max_steps

    n_poly = 3.0_dp   ! n = 3 (Eddington Standard Model for Relativistic Radiation/Degeneracy)
    dxi = 0.001_dp
    max_steps = 100000

    ! Initial series expansion around xi = 0 to bypass coordinate singularity:
    ! theta(xi) ~ 1 - xi^2 / 6 + n * xi^4 / 120
    xi = 0.001_dp
    theta = 1.0_dp - (xi**2)/6.0_dp + n_poly*(xi**4)/120.0_dp
    phi = -(xi/3.0_dp) + n_poly*(xi**3)/30.0_dp  ! phi = d(theta)/d(xi)

    print '(A, F5.2)', "Solving Lane-Emden equation for polytropic index n = ", n_poly

    do step = 1, max_steps
        if (theta <= 0.0_dp) exit

        ! RK4 Integrator for system: d(theta)/dxi = phi, d(phi)/dxi = -theta^n - 2*phi/xi
        call derivatives(xi, theta, phi, n_poly, k1_th, k1_ph)
        call derivatives(xi + 0.5_dp*dxi, theta + 0.5_dp*dxi*k1_th, phi + 0.5_dp*dxi*k1_ph, n_poly, k2_th, k2_ph)
        call derivatives(xi + 0.5_dp*dxi, theta + 0.5_dp*dxi*k2_th, phi + 0.5_dp*dxi*k2_ph, n_poly, k3_th, k3_ph)
        call derivatives(xi + dxi, theta + dxi*k3_th, phi + dxi*k3_ph, n_poly, k4_th, k4_ph)

        theta = theta + (dxi/6.0_dp)*(k1_th + 2.0_dp*k2_th + 2.0_dp*k3_th + k4_th)
        phi   = phi   + (dxi/6.0_dp)*(k1_ph + 2.0_dp*k2_ph + 2.0_dp*k3_ph + k4_ph)
        xi    = xi + dxi
    end do

    print '(A, F8.4)', "Stellar Surface xi_1 = ", xi
    print '(A, F8.4)', "Surface gradient |d(theta)/dxi| = ", abs(phi)
    print '(A, F8.4)', "Dimensionless Mass Ratio -xi_1^2 * theta'(xi_1) = ", xi**2 * abs(phi)

contains

    subroutine derivatives(x, th, ph, n, dth, dph)
        real(dp), intent(in) :: x, th, ph, n
        real(dp), intent(out) :: dth, dph
        dth = ph
        if (th > 0.0_dp) then
            dph = - (th**n) - (2.0_dp * ph / x)
        else
            dph = 0.0_dp
        end if
    end subroutine derivatives

end program solve_lane_emden

text:
Solutions to problems are to be submitted in legibly handwritten or in printed form. You will scan or photograph your work with your phone and submit it to the Assignments section of ASTB23 Quercus page. - Please put your student# at the top of the first page of every assignment. - Include the 3 last digits of your student number in the name of every submitted file.
Use your words, don’t just write a stream of symbols. Follow the method of solving problems discussed in the 1st tutorial: 1. Sketch of the situation. 2. Analytic transformations of equations. 3. Units check on intermediate results. 4. Numerical evaluation of results on a calculator. 5. Are my results plausible (e.g. of expected order-of-magnitude)? 6. title: Stellar Structure & The Lane-Emden Equation
text:
A spherical star in steady state balances inward gravitational force with outward gas/radiation pressure: \[\boxed{\frac{dP}{dr} = -\frac{G M(r) \rho(r)}{r^2}}\] where the enclosed mass \(M(r)\) satisfies the mass conservation equation: \[\frac{dM}{dr} = 4\pi r^2 \rho(r)\]
Combining these two equations by differentiating \(r^2 \frac{dP}{dr}\): \[\frac{1}{r^2} \frac{d}{dr}\left( \frac{r^2}{\rho} \frac{dP}{dr} \right) = -4\pi G \rho\]

text:
A spherical star in steady state balances inward gravitational force with outward gas/radiation pressure: \[\boxed{\frac{dP}{dr} = -\frac{G M(r) \rho(r)}{r^2}}\] where the enclosed mass \(M(r)\) satisfies the mass conservation equation: \[\frac{dM}{dr} = 4\pi r^2 \rho(r)\]

title: Stellar Structure & The Lane-Emden Equation
text:
2. Polytropic Equation of State
To close the structure equation without solving detailed energy transport, we introduce a polytropic relation: \[P = K \rho^\gamma = K \rho^{1 + 1/n}\] where \(n\) is the polytropic index (\(\gamma = 1 + \frac{1}{n}\)): * \(n = 1.5\) (\(\gamma = 5/3\)): Non-relativistic degenerate electron gas (White Dwarfs) or fully convective stars (Red Giants, Sun’s core). * \(n = 3.0\) (\(\gamma = 4/3\)): Relativistic degenerate electron gas (Chandrasekhar mass limit) or radiation-pressure dominated massive stars.

The Dimensionless Lane-Emden Equation
Define dimensionless density \(\theta(\xi)\) and radius \(\xi\): \[\rho(r) = \rho_c \theta^n(\xi), \qquad r = \alpha \xi\] where \(\alpha^2 = \frac{(n+1) K \rho_c^{1/n - 1}}{4\pi G}\).
Substituting into the hydrostatic equation yields the Lane-Emden Equation: \[\boxed{\frac{1}{\xi^2} \frac{d}{d\xi}\left( \xi^2 \frac{d\theta}{d\xi} \right) + \theta^n = 0}\] with boundary conditions at the stellar center (\(\xi = 0\)): \[\theta(0) = 1, \qquad \left. \frac{d\theta}{d\xi} \right|_{\xi=0} = 0\]
The stellar surface \(\xi_1\) is defined where density drops to zero: \(\theta(\xi_1) = 0\).
